t: In the House of Representatives, for the remainder of the 113th Congress, the provisions of H. Con. Res. 25 (113th Congress), as deemed in force by H. Res. 243 (113th Congress), shall remain in force to the extent its budgetary levels are not superseded by this subtitle or by further action of the House of Representatives.

fable.w: This section only keeps a congressional budget resolution in force within the House of Representatives for the remainder of the 113th Congress. The tempting reading is that "further action of the House" signals a procedural decision process, but the House is inside the federal government and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue. There is no comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or consultation with non-federal actors.
fable.s: shall remain in force to the extent its budgetary levels are not superseded by this subtitle or by further action of the House of Representatives

opus.w: This provision just keeps the levels in an earlier budget resolution in force within the House. The only actor named is the House of Representatives, which is part of the federal government. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue. The mention of "further action" by the House might look like a decision process, but it stays entirely inside the government.
opus.s: shall remain in force to the extent its budgetary levels are not superseded by this subtitle or by further action of the House of Representatives

qwen_chat.w: This section concerns internal congressional procedures and budgetary levels within the House of Representatives. Congress is part of the federal government, so actions taken by it do not constitute participation by outside parties. There is no mention of consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: In the House of Representatives, for the remainder of the 113th Congress, the provisions of H. Con. Res. 25 (113th Congress), as deemed in force by H. Res. 243 (113th Congress), shall remain in force to the extent its budgetary levels are not superseded by this subtitle or by further action of the House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "further action of the House of Representatives" implies a participatory process involving the public or other outside entities. However, the House of Representatives is part of the federal government (Congress), so any action taken by it is internal to the government. The text describes internal legislative procedures and budgetary levels, not consultation with or participation by non-federal parties.
